title: Target Groups and Individual Nodes
objective: Design inventory groups and host patterns that make deployment scope obvious.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 09 - Targeting Specific Nodes
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Inventory groups turn changing host addresses into stable operational roles such as webservers and databases. Plays should target those roles instead of a broad all pattern when only one tier needs a change.
Patterns can select a group, one host, an intersection, or an exclusion. The --limit option further narrows a playbook run without rewriting its hosts declaration.
Host variables describe real per-host differences. If the same value appears on many hosts, move it to group_vars rather than duplicating exceptions.
explanation.rule: Make the smallest correct target set visible before executing a change.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
- name: Configure only the web tier
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Show the selected host
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        var: inventory_hostname
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Design inventory groups and host patterns that make deployment scope obvious.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.

assignment.title: Target the Web Tier
assignment.brief: Write a play that reports each selected webserver hostname.
requirements: Include every named safety or behavior requirement.
assignment.solutionCode:
- name: Inspect the web tier
  hosts: webservers
  tasks:
    - name: Show selected host
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        var: inventory_hostname
assignment.outputCheckLabel: Artifact uses valid course-style YAML structure

lab.title: Prove targeting before changes
lab.setup: Start the disposable lab with npm run lab:up, then work from /workspace in the Terminal tab.
steps: Run the lesson play with --limit web01.
Run it again without the limit and compare host counts.
lab.success: The group selects two hosts and the limit selects only web01.
